title: Completed Codex review delegations leave orphaned sandbox process trees running for over an hour on DL560
outcome: Observed on DL560 on 2026-11-22, reported by DL560 Claude Live #233 and relayed by Opus2 #7476. Three Codex read-only review delegations (sessions 102, 104 and 106: B1-PAIR, B1-PAIR2 and B2-PAIR) all showed `completed` in termal_list_delegations. Each still left an orphan tree running about 9-80 minutes after its reviewer finished: a codex-linux-sandbox (ppid 1) running `node scripts/include-to-mod.mjs verify <base> .`, with a `rustfmt --emit stdout` child blocked on stdin. The trees sat in .tmp/pair-b1-28fe62ec, .tmp/pair-b1b-b15dcd57 and .tmp/pair-b2-e8cfd21b. They were removed by SIGTERM, which was itself a breach of Greg's no-kill rule and is reported separately. Delegation completion does not reap the provider sandbox's descendant processes, so they hold CPU, memory and the review checkout, which blocks its cleanup.
acceptance: When a delegation completes or is cancelled, no process descended from its provider (including a provider sandbox re-parented to init) keeps running; a behaviour test with a child that blocks on stdin shows the tree gone after completion, on Linux and on Windows. One limit: a process the kernel holds in uninterruptible sleep cannot be ended until it leaves that state; it and, on Linux, its descendants end once it leaves that state (ending those descendants earlier is tracked as w-bb7c3f95d686).

completion.summary:
Codex delegation children now run on an app-server of their own, and its whole process tree ends with the delegation, so a finished or cancelled review no longer leaves sandbox processes running.
- Linux: a keeper mode of the TermAl executable acts as child subreaper and is the server's parent. It kills and reaps all of its children until none is left, both when the server exits and when TermAl closes its control pipe. TermAl never kills a keeper that is still ending its tree.
- Windows: a kill-on-close job object.
- Where /proc is not in TermAl's PID namespace, the delegation fails at once and names the reason.
Behaviour tests use a provider fixture whose tool blocks on stdin under a setsid'd sandbox. They cover completion, cancellation, a server that exits by itself, a closed control pipe, the refusal, and the no-kill case.
